Fixes a boot failure on **Raspberry Pi Pico W**. No change to charge behaviour
from [v2.1](../../releases/tag/v2.1).

Same warnings as before: personal fork, developed and tested on one machine with
one powder, dispensing gunpowder charges - verify weights independently.

| File | Board | |
|---|---|---|
| `opentrickler-v2.2-pico2_w.uf2` | Raspberry Pi Pico **2** W (RP2350) | developed and tested on this |
| `opentrickler-v2.2-pico_w.uf2` | Raspberry Pi Pico W (RP2040) | **fix is unverified - see below** |

**No EEPROM change** - settings and profiles carry over from v2.0 or v2.1, and
there is no need to re-run Learn Powder.

## Pico W: motor error and a display that never came up

Reported against v2.1: works well on a Pico 2 W, but a Pico W throws a motor
error and the screen never loads. Both symptoms are one fault.

`driver_pio_init()` pinned the steppers to PIO block 0 and called
`pio_add_program()` **once per motor**. Both steppers run the same 7-instruction
program, so it used 14 of that block's 32 instruction words instead of 7. RP2350
has three PIO blocks and absorbed the waste; RP2040 has two, and the wifi chip's
SPI program claims room in one of them at startup. The second motor had nowhere
to load, `motor_init()` returned `MOTOR_INIT_PIO_ERR`, and the boot stopped
there - so the motors failed *and* nothing after that point ran, including the
display.

The program is now loaded once per PIO block with the offset shared between the
two motors, state machines are claimed without panicking, and if the preferred
block is full it falls back to any block with room.

**This fix has not been confirmed on hardware** - there is no RP2040 here to test
on. If a Pico W still misbehaves, the next thing to look at is RAM: it sits at
88% on that target against 44% on RP2350.

## Backup and restore was missing the Learn Powder settings

**Export Config** claimed to write every setting but never included
`/rest/learn_config`, so Time Goal, Bulk Safety Factor, Landing Sigma, confirm
target and the rest were silently dropped from a backup and lost on restore.
Now included. Import replays whatever the file contains, so older exports still
work - they just will not carry Learn settings that were never captured.

## Backup and restore is easier to find

The Export/Import buttons sat unlabelled at the bottom of the System Control
page, with nothing pointing at them - at least one user went looking and
concluded there was no import function. They now sit under a **Backup & Restore**
heading that says what gets saved, and the Profiles page notes that Export
Profile covers one profile while whole-machine backup lives on System Control.

Worth taking an export before any firmware update: a change to the stored format
resets settings to defaults on first boot.
